implementation: Remote install detects the final upgrade/uninstall operation and obtains all required helpers from the same pinned release tag.

Each asset is downloaded into a private canonical temporary directory, checked as a current-user-owned regular single-link file, verified against its own lowercase SHA-256, atomically renamed, made read-only, and rechecked before common.sh is sourced.

npm upgrade holds the external lifecycle locks while recovering residue, reading the existing managed package set, resolving one exact cohort, checking every required package, and prefetching with install scripts disabled.

The staged package update runs in the existing no-network bubblewrap transaction with npm offline mode and copy import; the opened validator fd 4 is exposed read-only at /run/dsh-enhanced-lifecycle-config.mjs after /tmp is hidden, and post-package structure, activation, state paths, symlink/hardlink/mount boundaries, and atomic rename are revalidated before commit.

Lifecycle coordination captures and revalidates the complete ancestor chain, then inherits and verifies parent-directory fd 3, the per-home lock fd 4, and the global rendezvous lock fd 5 across subprocess execution.
Before swap, the staged filesystem is flushed with sync -f and its directory fsynced; transaction and lock-parent directories are fsynced across rename, recovery, commit, and cleanup boundaries.
npm uninstall reuses the same locked and isolated lifecycle transaction but performs no npm registry lookup or pnpm store prefetch.

fixedFindings: Remote bootstrap initially trusted temporary paths too broadly; it now rejects non-canonical or symlink TMPDIR values, unsafe/foreign ancestors, group/other-writable private paths, replaced directories, and non-private or non-single-link assets before source.

Lifecycle coordination initially depended only on a pathname lock whose parent could change; it now binds the ancestor chain and parent fd, anchors the per-home lock through that fd, adds a root-sticky-/tmp rendezvous lock, and rechecks identities around critical renames.

A package operation could introduce or retarget an external node_modules symlink after the pre-scan; the post-package scan now permits only unchanged pre-existing package links and rejects new, changed, or newly dangling links before commit.
An uninstall activation failure could expose archive work in the live home; archive creation now remains inside staged evidence and the original home remains unchanged on failure.

npm selector and release pin parsing accepted insufficiently narrow or partially updated states; exact SemVer/dist-tag resolution, complete same-version cohort checks, paired lifecycle sentinels, and atomic three-asset release pin validation now fail closed.

Recovery and canonical-home aliases had path/identity gaps before registry access; recovery now uses physical paths under the held lock and returns for operator confirmation without registry or store access.

The validator was previously addressed through the logical DSH_HOME under default /tmp, which the sandbox then hid; the final implementation passes the already-open validator as fd 4 and mounts it read-only under isolated /run before executing validation.

limitations: The npm and pnpm executables in the high-fidelity verification were recording substitutes; no package was published and no real npm registry state was changed.
The mutable main copy of install-npm.sh remains outside the three downloaded asset digests; immutable tag policy and repository administration remain part of the release trust root.
Only Linux web/autonomy offline lifecycle is supported. Lark and supervised resident-service stop, restart, readiness, and rollback are not delivered.
This evidence does not claim model quality, external credentials, long-running service lifecycle, or full WP17 completion.
